description:
Start a 2FA challenge that grants the authenticated user permission to perform a sensitive action. The 2FA must complete on a channel DIFFERENT from the user's last login channel (the backend enforces this). On success a grant is stored keyed by the user id and action_type; middleware on the protected endpoint reads the grant and allows the mutation.

Destructive action types (api_key_create, api_key_revoke, api_key_regenerate, api_key_view, account_delete, phone_remove, email_remove, phone_primary, email_primary, revocation_bulk, domain_remove, profile_delete) are capped at 5min TTL and forced single-use by server policy. A step-up for revocation_bulk, phone_remove, email_remove, domain_remove, profile_delete or account_delete is bound to `targets` — the exact ids the protected call will carry. Configuration scopes (settings_write, profile_update, templates_write) allow up to 24h TTL and caller-chosen single_use — useful for agents making multiple settings mutations in one session.

Agent usage: (1) Attempt the sensitive call; if you get `403 2fa_required` note the `action_type`. (2) Call start_2fa_for_action with that action_type and a channel different from the login channel. (3) Present the challenge: on telegram/whatsapp pass `deep_link` to render_auth_link; on sms show `sms_message` and the number to send it to; on email check the response first: with more than one verified email and no `email_id` given, it answers 200 with `requires_email_selection: true` and `available_emails` — NO session was started and nothing was sent, so ask the user which address and call again with `email_id` rather than telling them to open a mailbox. Never hand `qr_text` to a link renderer — it is the link already rendered as QR art. Print it verbatim inside a fenced code block only when a real terminal needs the QR. (4) Call wait_for_2fa until the session is verified. (5) Retry the original sensitive call.

The user does not see tool results — most clients fold them away, render_auth_link's output included. Before you wait or poll, put what the user must act on into your own reply text: the link itself (not a sentence announcing it), the SMS text and number, or a note to check their inbox.

ACCESS: needs a Proof account. Authenticate this client (Claude Code: /mcp → Authenticate), then call this tool again. start_login does NOT open this tool.

action_type.description: The sensitive action the 2FA grant will authorize: any action type the API documents. The server caps each by its policy: destructive types (e.g. api_key_*, *_remove, revocation_bulk, account_delete) to 5 min TTL and single use; configuration scopes (e.g. settings_write, webhook_write) up to 24h with caller-chosen single_use.

channel.description: Channel for the 2FA challenge — must differ from the user's last login channel

email_id.description: Optional: specific UserEmail id for email-channel 2FA

phone_id.description: Optional: specific UserPhone id for phone-channel 2FA

single_use.description: Whether the grant is consumed on first use. Server forces true for destructive action types. Defaults to true.

targets.description: The ids the step-up is FOR — the grant is bound to exactly these and refused for any other request (`reason: target_mismatch`). revocation_bulk: the asset id you will pass to revoke_asset (one code per asset); phone_remove / email_remove: the phone or email record id; domain_remove: the domain id; profile_delete: the sub-account id; account_delete: your own user id (get_current_user). Leave out for the other action types.

ttl_seconds.description: Requested grant lifetime in seconds. Server caps to 300s for destructive action types, 86400s for configuration scopes. Defaults to 300 if omitted.

name: start_2fa_for_action

available_emails.description: The addresses the code may go to; call again with one of their ids as `email_id`

deep_link.description: Opens Telegram or WhatsApp with what the person sends (`telegram`, `whatsapp`)

email.description: The address the code went to, masked (`email` only)

email_sent.description: `true` when the code was emailed (`email` only)

instructions.description: One line telling the person what to do

qr_text.description: UTF-8 text QR for `deep_link`, for terminal/agent rendering

requires_email_selection.description: Always `true`: no session was started, pick an address and start again

second_method_recommended.description: Present (true) when the step-up uses the channel the account signed in with, because the account has no other; adding a second channel is recommended

sms_code.description: The short code the person texts (`sms` only)

sms_dids.description: Our SMS numbers, one entry per region and always all three. A region with no number configured carries an empty `did` and no QR code.
